newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday June 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday June 3.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Foreign minister Lamberto Dini, attending a meeting of European Union foreign ministers in Luxembourg, said Italy wanted European economic and monetary union (EMU) to proceed on time even though he thought an extra year of preparation would be helpful for everyone. According to Dini what the European Community really needs to do now is check how strongly Europe wants monetary union (all).

* Prime minister Romano Prodi said he would prefer his parliamentary ally the hard-left Communist Refoundation party to be part of his centre-left government because it would show common commitment and it would mean collective responsibility (all).

* Giorgio Fossa, chairman of employers' association Confindustria, said the association would not sit down with government and unions to discuss welfare reforms unless partial pension reforms made two years ago were included. Fossa also complained one-off government measures that did not solve any problems (all).

* The International Monetary Fund officially welcomed Italy's choice to re-enter the European exchange rate mechanism at 990 against the German mark but said currency stability would only happen if the government reformed welfare state spending (La Repubblica).
* A study by Italian research institute Isco showed the country's business activities' perspective for the future were seen in a less pessimistic way (Sole 24 Ore).
* Federico Nucci, commercial director of Italian state airline Alitalia, said the company could return to profit in 1997 (Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
